SMTO-SKL-0158 — GitHub didn't accept your saved sign-in token

GUID: 60ef5161-fccc-5b1b-8041-85a664274f92
Slug: github-reauthentication-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub turned down the token saved for your account. Tokens can expire or be deleted on GitHub. Because GitHub refused the request, it didn't change anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On github.com, open your account's Settings, then Developer settings, then Personal access tokens, and check whether the token has expired or been deleted. GitHub refuses tokens that have expired or been removed.
  2. Create a new token for the same GitHub user, giving it the same repositories and permissions as before. Keeping the same access means SMTO can do what it did before, and no more.
  3. In SMTO, open Parameter Store, select your GitHub account entry, open Value, select Reveal & edit value, replace only the token, and select Save. SMTO reads the token from this entry each time it contacts GitHub.
  4. Ask SMTO to check your GitHub connection, then repeat your request. The check confirms GitHub accepts the new token before you try the real request.

What success looks like

  • The connection check shows your GitHub login as verified and your request completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the token into the chat; keep it only in Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHub returned HTTP 401 (not classified as a rate limit) for the selected account's token, so the request was rejected.

What this means

  • GitHub returns HTTP 401 outside rate-limit classification. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • GitHub returns HTTP 401 outside rate-limit classification.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact profile and safe provider status without exposing the token.

How to fix it

  • GitHubClient.error maps HTTP 401 to reauthentication_required. Issue a new PAT for the same GitHub user with the same repository selection and permissions, replace only the token field in that exact GitHub Account profile in Parameter Store, then run github.connection_status.
  • Replace the expired or rejected token in the exact GitHub Account profile in Parameter Store, preserving the intended principal and repository selection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The same intended principal has a valid supported token before further work.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
